sources.finding: Codex local CLI and Cloud usage count toward applicable Codex allowances; the plan allowance is not a documented fixed RPM guarantee.
API limits can apply to requests, tokens, organizations, projects and model families. Public API limits do not establish this signed-in Codex account's limit.
Fast mode targets latency and has pay-as-you-go pricing; a latency improvement is not evidence of a proportional admission-limit increase.
Latest stable release, published 2026-11-06; installed separately with npm archive integrity verification.
Latest npm alpha at lookup, published 2026-11-07; installed separately, not chosen for main collection.
The generic HTTP 429 mapping retains status/request tracking but drops most response body/header detail. A generic RPC 429 does not identify the precise limiter.
Server retry advice affects scheduling, including transport fallback. This does not justify automatic replay of uncertain scientific requests.
CODEX_SQLITE_HOME is the supported database-only override; confirmed also at the old 0.159.0-alpha.3 tag. Authentication HOME need not change.
Reports 429 and long shared cooldown deadlines despite remaining weekly allowance on 0.166.0. It is corroborating symptom evidence, not proof of our root cause.
Reports inference 429 with allowance remaining and explicitly leaves the precise rejecting condition unresolved.
Reports gpt-5.6-sol low effort failing while medium succeeds. Limits or availability may depend on model/effort.
Reports no supported zero-advertised-tools option despite many disabled features. Our local wire capture independently shows additional tool definitions and version differences.

network.conclusion: Proxy-generated 429 is possible per runtime guidance but unproven; no proxy bypass was attempted.
